tools.description:
List legacy aggregated compressed-token balances for a Solana owner with bounded pagination. Uses Alchemy's Solana Photon/ZK Compression indexer.

Best for:
  - you need to check wallet balances, token holdings, or portfolio value.

Not recommended for:
  - you need protocol-level DeFi data (use get_tvl_protocols instead).

Args:
  - network (string, optional): Alchemy Solana network slug.. Default: "solana-mainnet". Values: solana-mainnet, solana-devnet.
  - owner (string, required): owner.
  - mint (string, optional): mint.
  - cursor (string, optional): Photon pagination cursor returned by a previous response..
  - limit (integer, optional): Maximum records to return (1-100).. Default: 100.

Returns:
  JSON object with wallet data including: address, chain, token balances with symbols and USD values.

Example:
  {"network":"solana-mainnet","owner":"value"}

Common mistakes:
  - Missing required parameters: owner. All are mandatory.

Error Handling:
  - Rate limit: wait 60s and retry.
  - Invalid params: check Args section above.
  - Network error: retry with exponential backoff.

tools.name: alchemy_solana_search_assets
tools.title: Solana Search Assets
tools.description:
Search Solana assets using owner, token type, creator, authority, collection, compression, and royalty filters. Uses Alchemy's Solana Digital Asset Standard (DAS) API.

Best for:
  - you need to look up coins, tokens, or NFTs by name or keyword.

Not recommended for:
  - a more specific tool exists for your exact data need.

Args:
  - network (string, optional): Alchemy Solana network slug.. Default: "solana-mainnet". Values: solana-mainnet, solana-devnet.
  - ownerAddress (string, required): Owner public key. Required by Alchemy's DAS proxy..
  - tokenType (string, optional): tokenType. Default: "all". Values: fungible, nonFungible, regularNFT, compressedNFT, all.
  - sortBy (object, optional): Alchemy DAS asset sort field and direction..
  - page (integer, optional): One-indexed result page.. Default: 1.
  - limit (integer, optional): Maximum results to return (bounded at 1,000).. Default: 100.
  - before (string, optional): Return records before this cursor..
  - after (string, optional): Return records after this cursor..
  - cursor (string, optional): Pagination cursor returned by a previous response..
  - negate (boolean, optional): negate. Default: false.
  - conditionType (string, optional): conditionType. Default: "all". Values: all, any.
  - creatorAddress (string, optional): creatorAddress.
  - creatorVerified (boolean, optional): creatorVerified.
  - authorityAddress (string, optional): authorityAddress.
  - delegate (string, optional): delegate.
  - frozen (boolean, optional): frozen.
  - burnt (boolean, optional): burnt.
  - compressed (boolean, optional): compressed.
  - compressible (boolean, optional): compressible.
  - supplyMint (string, optional): supplyMint.
  - royaltyTargetType (string, optional): royaltyTargetType. Values: creators, fanout, single.
  - royaltyTarget (string, optional): royaltyTarget.
  - name (string, optional): Asset-name substring..
  - jsonUri (string, optional): Exact JSON metadata URI..
  - royaltyAmount (integer, optional): royaltyAmount.
  - supply (integer, optional): supply.
  - grouping (array, optional): Strict [groupKey, groupValue] tuple..
  - options (object, optional): Optional DAS response flags such as showUnverifiedCollections, showCollectionMetadata, showZeroBalance, showInscription, and showFungible..

Returns:

tools.name: archive_get_basis_history
tools.title: Archive Get Basis History
tools.description:
Get historical spot-vs-futures BASIS snapshots for one base coin across venues from the Hive Archive. Each row: exchange, base_coin, spot_price, futures_price, basis_rate (fraction), annualized_basis, timestamp — the basis fields were computed at collection time from the venue's own spot and futures quotes.

Args:
  - base_coin (string, required): base asset ticker, e.g. "BTC", "ETH", "SOL" (case-insensitive; uppercased server-side).
  - exchange (string, optional): one venue, matched case-insensitively (e.g. "Binance", "okx"). Omit for all venues.
  - from (string, optional): ISO 8601 inclusive lower bound.
  - to (string, optional): ISO 8601 inclusive upper bound.
  - limit (integer, optional): max rows (1-500, default 100), newest first.

Returns:
  Bounded JSON envelope: { "provider", "dataset", "runtime_status", "fetched_at", "note", "filters", "order", "returnedCount", "may_have_more", "rows" }. Rows are newest-first; may_have_more true means the limit was hit — page older data by setting "to" below the oldest returned timestamp.

Examples:
  - { "base_coin": "BTC", "from": "2026-05-01T00:00:00Z", "limit": 300 } — BTC basis regime since May.
  - { "base_coin": "SOL", "exchange": "Binance" } — recent SOL basis snapshots on Binance.

Use when:
  - You are studying cash-and-carry yield history or basis blowouts/compressions over time
  - You need basis context around a historical funding or liquidation event

Don't use when:
  - You need LIVE basis or dated-futures term structure right now (use ccxt_ mark/index tools or hyperliquid tools)
  - You need current cross-venue funding instead of basis (use archive_get_funding_history for history, ccxt_fetch_funding_rates_multi for now)

tools.name: archive_get_coverage
tools.title: Archive Get Coverage
tools.description:
Discover what the Hive Archive holds: the all-time venue list (33 CEX+DEX funding venues) and earliest/latest timestamps per dataset (funding settlements, open interest, basis, long/short ratio, liquidations). Funding extremes are global; futures-dataset extremes are probed for one base coin (default "BTC" — verified to match the global extremes) because those tables are indexed by (base_coin, timestamp). Examples:
  - {} — full coverage picture with BTC probes.
  - { "base_coin": "DOGE" } — how far back DOGE futures datasets go.

Use when:
  - Before a history query, to learn venue names and how far back each dataset reaches
  - "Which exchanges does the funding archive cover?" / "since when is there OI history?"

Don't use when:

tools.name: archive_get_funding_history
tools.title: Archive Get Funding History
tools.description:
Get historical perp funding-rate SETTLEMENTS for one base coin across up to 33 CEX+DEX venues from the Hive Archive (archive since 2023-11; 9.8M settlement rows). Each row is one settled funding event: exchange, symbol, base_coin, rate (raw per-interval fraction), interval_hours, settled_at — plus a derived funding_annualized computed honestly from that row's own interval (rate * 8760 / interval_hours; null when the interval is unknown, never a guessed 8h default).

Args:
  - base_coin (string, required): base asset ticker, e.g. "BTC", "ETH", "SOL" (case-insensitive; uppercased server-side).
  - exchange (string, optional): one venue, matched case-insensitively (e.g. "Binance", "okx"). Omit for all venues.
  - from (string, optional): ISO 8601 inclusive lower bound.
  - to (string, optional): ISO 8601 inclusive upper bound.
  - limit (integer, optional): max rows (1-500, default 100), newest first.

Returns:
  Bounded JSON envelope: { "provider", "dataset", "runtime_status", "fetched_at", "note", "filters", "order", "returnedCount", "may_have_more", "rows" }. Rows are newest-first; may_have_more true means the limit was hit — page older data by setting "to" below the oldest returned timestamp.

Examples:
  - { "base_coin": "BTC", "from": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z", "limit": 200 } — BTC settlements across venues since 2024.
  - { "base_coin": "ETH", "exchange": "Hyperliquid", "limit": 100 } — recent ETH settlements on one venue.

Use when:
  - "BTC funding history across exchanges since 2024" — long-window, cross-venue funding studies
  - You are computing realized carry, funding regime shifts, or venue funding divergence over time

tools.name: archive_get_open_interest_history
tools.title: Archive Get Open Interest History
tools.description:
Get historical perp open-interest snapshots for one base coin across venues from the Hive Archive (2.1M rows). Each row: exchange, base_coin, symbol (venue-native contract), open_interest_value (venue-reported OI as collected), timestamp. Retention is shorter than funding — call archive_get_coverage for exact per-dataset depth.

Args:
  - base_coin (string, required): base asset ticker, e.g. "BTC", "ETH", "SOL" (case-insensitive; uppercased server-side).
  - exchange (string, optional): one venue, matched case-insensitively (e.g. "Binance", "okx"). Omit for all venues.
  - from (string, optional): ISO 8601 inclusive lower bound.
  - to (string, optional): ISO 8601 inclusive upper bound.
  - limit (integer, optional): max rows (1-500, default 100), newest first.

Returns:
  Bounded JSON envelope: { "provider", "dataset", "runtime_status", "fetched_at", "note", "filters", "order", "returnedCount", "may_have_more", "rows" }. Rows are newest-first; may_have_more true means the limit was hit — page older data by setting "to" below the oldest returned timestamp.

Examples:
  - { "base_coin": "ETH", "from": "2026-07-18T00:00:00Z", "to": "2026-08-18T00:00:00Z" } — ETH OI over the last month.
  - { "base_coin": "BTC", "exchange": "OKX", "limit": 500 } — recent BTC OI snapshots on OKX.

Use when:
  - "ETH open interest history last month" — OI trend and buildup/unwind analysis over time
  - You are correlating OI changes with funding or liquidation events across venues

Don't use when:
  - You need CURRENT open interest (use ccxt_fetch_open_interest_multi or get_open_interest)
  - You need one venue's own OI history endpoint shape (use get_open_interest_history via CCXT)

tools.name: ccxt_fetch_convert_quote
tools.title: CCXT Fetch Convert Quote
tools.description:
Fetch a conversion quote (estimated rate) for converting between currencies on an exchange via CCXT.

Returns the estimated exchange rate and output amount for converting one currency to another using the exchange's built-in convert/swap feature. Quote is typically valid for a short window (10-30 seconds).

Args:
  - exchange (string, required): Exchange ID with convert feature. Supported: "binance", "bybit", "okx".
  - fromCode (string, required): Source currency code (e.g., "BTC", "ETH", "USDT").
  - toCode (string, required): Target currency code (e.g., "USDT", "BTC", "ETH").
  - amount (number, optional): Amount to convert in source currency. Some exchanges require this.

Returns:
  JSON object with quote:
  {
    "fromCode": string,
    "toCode": string,
    "fromAmount": number,
    "toAmount": number,
    "rate": number,
    "inverseRate": number,
    "expiry": number,
    "info": {...}
  }

Examples:
  - Get BTC to USDT quote: {"exchange": "binance", "fromCode": "BTC", "toCode": "USDT", "amount": 1}
  - Get ETH to BTC quote: {"exchange": "okx", "fromCode": "ETH", "toCode": "BTC", "amount": 10}

Use when:
  - You need a conversion rate estimate between two currencies
  - You want to compare convert rates vs spot trading rates
  - You're helping a user decide whether to convert or trade
  - You need to preview conversion output before execution

Don't use when:
  - You need spot market prices (use ccxt_fetch_ticker)
  - You want to execute the conversion (requires auth)
  - You need historical exchange rates (use ccxt_fetch_ohlcv)

Error Handling:
  - Not all exchanges support convert quotes
  - Some exchanges require amount parameter
  - Quote expires quickly — re-fetch before execution
  - Unsupported currency pairs return error with available options

tools.name: ccxt_fetch_funding_rates_multi
tools.title: Fetch Funding Rates Across Venues
tools.description:
Fetch the current perpetual funding rate for ONE symbol across SEVERAL exchanges in a single call. Venues are queried with bounded concurrency and isolated per-venue error handling: every venue returns its own row with a runtime_status, so one failing/geo-blocked venue never hides the others.

Args:
  - venues (array, required): 1-10 CCXT exchange ids, e.g. ["binance", "bybit", "okx"].
  - symbol (string, required): Unified perp symbol including settle currency, e.g. "BTC/USDT:USDT".

Returns:
  JSON object:
  {
    "symbol": string,
    "venueCount": number,
    "okCount": number,          // venues that returned data
    "rows": [{
      "exchange": string,
      "runtime_status": "ok" | "invalid_input" | "rate_limited" | "degraded" | "failing" | ...,
      "data"?: {...},           // unified CCXT funding-rate record when ok
      "error"?: string          // actionable provider error otherwise
    }]
  }

Examples:
  - Compare BTC funding on three venues: {"venues":["binance","bybit","okx"],"symbol":"BTC/USDT:USDT"}

Use when:
  - You are hunting cross-venue funding divergence / carry for one market
  - You want funding for the same perp on several CEXes without N separate calls

Don't use when:
  - You need ALL symbols on one venue (use ccxt_fetch_funding_rates)
  - You need predicted cross-venue funding from Hyperliquid's feed (use hyperliquid_get_predicted_fundings)

tools.name: ccxt_fetch_mark_prices
tools.title: CCXT Fetch Mark Prices
tools.description:
Fetch mark prices for perpetual/futures contracts from an exchange via CCXT.

Returns the mark price used by exchanges for margin calculations and liquidations. Mark prices are derived from index prices and are less susceptible to manipulation than last traded prices.

Args:
  - exchange (string, required): Exchange ID with derivatives. Supported: "binance", "bybit", "okx", "bitget", "gate".
  - symbols (array, required): Array of 1-100 contract symbols (e.g., ["BTC/USDT:USDT", "ETH/USDT:USDT"]).

Returns:
  JSON object keyed by symbol:
  {
    "BTC/USDT:USDT": {
      "symbol": string,
      "timestamp": number,
      "datetime": string,
      "markPrice": number,
      "indexPrice": number,
      "interestRate": number,
      "estimatedSettlePrice": number,
      "info": {...}
    },
    ...
  }

Examples:
  - Get specific mark prices: {"exchange": "bybit", "symbols": ["BTC/USDT:USDT", "ETH/USDT:USDT"]}

Use when:
  - You need mark prices for liquidation/margin calculations
  - You want to compare mark price vs last price (premium/discount)
  - You're monitoring basis between spot and derivatives
  - You need batch mark prices for multiple contracts

Don't use when:
  - You need spot prices (use ccxt_fetch_tickers)
  - You need mark price history (use ccxt_fetch_mark_ohlcv)
  - You need funding rates (use ccxt_fetch_funding_rates)

Error Handling:
  - Only derivatives exchanges support mark prices
  - Symbols must include settle currency (e.g., BTC/USDT:USDT)
  - Not all exchanges support batch fetchMarkPrices

Hive safety bound: symbols is required and accepts at most 100 entries; unbounded all-market reads are rejected.

tools.name: ccxt_fetch_open_interest_multi
tools.title: Fetch Open Interest Across Venues
tools.description:
Fetch current open interest for ONE symbol across SEVERAL exchanges in a single call. Venues are queried with bounded concurrency and isolated per-venue error handling: every venue returns its own row with a runtime_status, so partial results always flow.

Args:
  - venues (array, required): 1-10 CCXT exchange ids, e.g. ["binance", "bybit", "okx"].
  - symbol (string, required): Unified perp symbol including settle currency, e.g. "BTC/USDT:USDT".

Returns:
  JSON object:
  {
    "symbol": string,
    "venueCount": number,
    "okCount": number,
    "rows": [{
      "exchange": string,
      "runtime_status": "ok" | "invalid_input" | "rate_limited" | "degraded" | "failing" | ...,
      "data"?: {...},           // unified CCXT open-interest record when ok
      "error"?: string
    }]
  }

Examples:
  - Compare ETH OI on three venues: {"venues":["binance","bybit","okx"],"symbol":"ETH/USDT:USDT"}

Use when:
  - You are sizing where open interest is concentrated across venues for one market
  - You want a cross-venue OI snapshot without N separate calls

Don't use when:
  - You need OI history on one venue (use ccxt_fetch_open_interest_history)
  - You need protocol-level aggregate OI (use defillama_get_open_interest)

tools.name: codex_get_token_bars

tools.description:
Get token-level aggregated OHLCV candlestick data using Codex by Defined.fi. Unlike pair-level bars, this aggregates price data across ALL DEX pairs for a token, giving a holistic view of the token's price action.

Args:
  - tokenAddress (string, required): Token contract address.
  - networkId (number, required): Blockchain network ID.
  - from (number, required): Start Unix timestamp (seconds).
  - to (number, required): End Unix timestamp (seconds).
  - resolution (string, required): Candle timeframe. Values: 1, 5, 15, 30, 60, 240, 720, 1D, 7D.
  - countback (number, optional): Number of bars counting back from 'to'.
  - currencyCode (string, optional): Quote currency code. Values: USD or TOKEN.
  - removeEmptyBars (boolean, optional): Remove candles with zero trades.
  - removeLeadingNullValues (boolean, optional): Strip leading nulls.
  - statsType (string, optional): FILTERED or UNFILTERED.

Returns:
  JSON with arrays: o (open), h (high), l (low), c (close), t (timestamps), volume, buyVolume, sellVolume, buyers, sellers, buys, sells, traders, transactions, liquidity, and full token metadata.

Examples:
  - WETH 1h candles: {"tokenAddress": "0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2", "networkId": 1, "resolution": "60", "from": 1700000000, "to": 1700086400}

tools.name: codex_get_windowed_pair_stats
tools.title: Codex Get Windowed Pair Stats
tools.description:
Get windowed DEX pair statistics via the schema-only getDetailedStats Codex query: per-window (5m/1h/4h/12h/24h) transactions, volume, unique buyers/sellers/traders, and buy/sell splits for one pair. Complements get_detailed_stats (which uses the duration-based getDetailedPairStats query) with the windowSizes-based API.

Args:
  - networkId (number, required): Blockchain network ID.
  - pairAddress (string, required): DEX pair contract address (combined internally to "address:networkId").
  - windowSizes (string[], optional): min5 | hour1 | hour4 | hour12 | day1. Default: ["day1"].
  - statsType (string, optional): FILTERED | UNFILTERED.
  - tokenOfInterest (string, optional): token0 | token1.
  - bucketCount (number, optional): Historical buckets per window.
  - timestamp (number, optional): Historical anchor (Unix seconds).

Returns:
  JSON object: { "pairId", "tokenOfInterest", "statsType", "stats_min5"?, "stats_hour1"?, "stats_hour4"?, "stats_hour12"?, "stats_day1"? } — each window carries transactions/volume/buyers/sellers/traders/buys/sells/buyVolume/sellVolume currentValue metrics.

Examples:
  - USDC/WETH day + hour windows: { "networkId": 1, "pairAddress": "0xB4e16d0168e52d35CaCD2c6185b44281Ec28C9Dc", "windowSizes": ["day1", "hour1"] }

Use when:
  - You need multi-window trader/volume breakdowns for one DEX pair in one call.

Don't use when:
  - You need bucketed duration charts (use get_detailed_stats).
  - You need token-level (not pair-level) stats (use codex_get_detailed_token_stats).

Get time-series chart data for a prediction market using Codex by Defined.fi. Returns outcome probabilities, volume, and liquidity over time for building market charts.

Args:
  - marketId (string, required): Prediction market ID.
  - from (number, required): Start Unix timestamp.
  - to (number, required): End Unix timestamp.
  - resolution (string, required): Time resolution for bars (min1, min5, min15, min30, hour1, hour4, hour12, day1, week1).
  - countback (number, optional): Number of bars counting back from 'to'.
  - removeEmptyBars (boolean, optional): Omit bars with no activity.

Returns:
  JSON with time-series arrays: timestamps, outcome probabilities, volume, liquidity, and open interest per bar.

Use when:
  - You need to chart how a market's probabilities have moved over time.
  - You want volume and liquidity trends for a prediction market.

Don't use when:
  - You need current stats only — use codex_prediction_market_stats.

tools.name: codex_prediction_market_price
tools.title: Codex Prediction Market Price
tools.description:
Get current outcome prices for a prediction market using Codex by Defined.fi. Returns best bid/ask and last trade price for each outcome.

Args:
  - marketId (string, required): Prediction market ID.
  - timestamp (number, optional): Unix timestamp for historical price. If omitted, returns latest price.

Returns:
  JSON with market ID, timestamp, and per-outcome prices including bestBid, bestAsk, and lastTradePrice in both collateral token and USD.

Use when:
  - You need the current price/probability of a prediction market's outcomes.
  - You want to check bid/ask spreads for a market.
  - You need a point-in-time price snapshot.

Don't use when:
  - You need price history over time — use codex_prediction_market_bars.
  - You need full market stats — use codex_prediction_market_stats.

tools.name: codex_prediction_token_holders
tools.title: Codex Prediction Token Holders
tools.description:
Get token holder data for prediction market outcome tokens using Codex by Defined.fi. Shows who holds positions in specific market outcomes.

  - include_address_label (boolean, optional): Include known address labels (e.g., exchange names). Default: false.

Returns:

Examples:
  - Top traders of a token on Ethereum: {"network": "eth", "address": "0x6921b130d297cc43754afba22e5eac0fbf8db75b"}
  - Top by unrealized PnL: {"network": "eth", "address": "0x...", "sort": "unrealized_pnl_usd_desc"}
  - Top 50 traders: {"network": "bsc", "address": "0x...", "traders": "50"}

Use when:
  - You need to identify the most profitable traders of a token
  - You're tracking smart money and whale trading activity
  - You want to see who's buying/selling the most of a token
  - You're analyzing trading patterns for a specific token

Don't use when:

Fetch live data from an allowlisted public crypto API when no dedicated Hive tool covers the source. The long-tail escape hatch so you are never dead-ended.

tools.name: get_coin_ohlc_range
tools.title: Get Coin Ohlc Range
tools.description:
Get OHLC (Open, High, Low, Close) candlestick chart data for a coin within a specific time range from CoinGecko.

Returns candlestick data for technical analysis and charting between specified UNIX timestamps. Essential for building candlestick charts and performing technical analysis.

Args:
  - id (string, required): CoinGecko coin ID (e.g., "bitcoin", "ethereum"). Use coingecko_get_coins_list to find valid IDs.
  - vs_currency (string, required): Target currency for prices (e.g., "usd", "eur", "btc").
  - from (number, required): Start time as UNIX timestamp (e.g., 1704067200 for Jan 1, 2024).
  - to (number, required): End time as UNIX timestamp.
  - interval (string, required): Data interval for candles. Options: "daily", "hourly".

Returns:
  JSON array of OHLC candle data:
  [
    [1704067200000, 42000.00, 42500.00, 41800.00, 42200.00],  // [timestamp_ms, open, high, low, close]
    [1704153600000, 42200.00, 42800.00, 42100.00, 42600.00],
    [1704240000000, 42600.00, 43000.00, 42400.00, 42900.00],
    ...
  ]

  Each candle array contains:
  - [0] timestamp: UNIX timestamp in milliseconds
  - [1] open: Opening price for the period
  - [2] high: Highest price during the period
  - [3] low: Lowest price during the period
  - [4] close: Closing price for the period

Examples:
  - Bitcoin daily candles Jan 2024: {"id": "bitcoin", "vs_currency": "usd", "from": 1704067200, "to": 1706745600, "interval": "daily"}
  - Ethereum hourly candles: {"id": "ethereum", "vs_currency": "usd", "from": 1705312800, "to": 1705399200, "interval": "hourly"}
  - Solana Q4 2023 daily: {"id": "solana", "vs_currency": "usd", "from": 1696118400, "to": 1704067200, "interval": "daily"}

Use when:
  - You need candlestick data for charting
  - You're performing technical analysis
  - You need OHLC values for a specific time range
  - You're building trading charts or indicators

Don't use when:
  - You only need closing prices (use coingecko_get_coin_market_chart_range)
  - You need volume data (use coingecko_get_coin_market_chart_range)
  - You need current price only (use coingecko_get_simple_price)
  - You have a contract address instead of coin ID

Error Handling:
  - Returns 404 if coin ID not found
  - Time range should be reasonable for the interval
  - Hourly data may be limited to recent periods
  - Rate limited to 10-50 calls/minute depending on API plan

tools.description:
Get CoinGecko's current supply breakdown for a coin, including tracked non-circulating wallets. Requires a CoinGecko Analyst, Lite, Pro, or Enterprise API plan.

tools.name: get_contract_market_chart
tools.title: Get Contract Market Chart
tools.description:
Get historical price chart data for a token by contract address from CoinGecko.

Returns historical price, market cap, and volume data points for a token identified by its contract address. Uses a days parameter for the lookback period. Use this when you have a contract address and need a simple time-based chart.

Args:
  - id (string, required): Asset platform ID (e.g., "ethereum", "polygon-pos", "arbitrum-one", "binance-smart-chain").

  - vs_currency (string, required): Target currency (e.g., "usd", "eur", "btc").
  - days (string, required): Data up to N days ago. Any integer or "max".
  - interval (string, optional): Data interval. Options: "5m", "hourly", "daily". Auto-selected if omitted.
  - precision (string, optional): Decimal precision. Options: "full", "0"-"18".

Returns:
  JSON object with prices, market_caps, and total_volumes arrays of [timestamp_ms, value] pairs.

Examples:
  - USDT 30-day chart: {"id": "ethereum", "contract_address": "0xdac17f958d2ee523a2206206994597c13d831ec7", "vs_currency": "usd", "days": "30"}
  - Daily interval: {"id": "ethereum", "contract_address": "0xa0b86991c6218b36c1d19d4a2e9eb0ce3606eb48", "vs_currency": "usd", "days": "90", "interval": "daily"}

Use when:
  - You need a price chart for a token by contract address with a simple days lookback
  - You don't need exact start/end timestamps

Don't use when:
  - You need a specific date range (use coingecko_get_contract_market_chart_range)
  - You know the CoinGecko coin ID (use coingecko_get_coin_market_chart)
  - You need current price only (use coingecko_get_simple_token_price)

Error Handling:
  - Returns 404 if token not found on specified platform
  - Auto-granularity: longer ranges = larger intervals
  - Rate limited based on API plan

tools.title: Get Funding Rate History
tools.description:
Fetch funding rate history for perpetual futures contracts.

Best for:
  - you need perpetual futures funding rate data.

Not recommended for:
  - a more specific tool exists for your exact data need.

Args:
  - exchange (string, required): Exchange ID. Top exchanges: binance, coinbase, kraken, bybit, okx. 100+ exchanges supported via CCXT..
  - symbol (string, optional): Perpetual contract symbol (optional).
  - since (number, optional): Timestamp in milliseconds to fetch history since.
  - limit (integer, optional): Number of funding rate entries to return.

Returns:
  JSON object with the requested data. Use get_api_endpoint_schema for the full response schema.

Example:
  {"exchange":"kraken"}

Common mistakes:
  - Omitting the exchange parameter. Always specify which exchange (e.g., 'kraken', 'binance').
  - Missing required parameters: exchange. All are mandatory.

Error Handling:
  - Rate limit: wait 60s and retry.
  - Invalid params: check Args section above.
  - Network error: retry with exponential backoff.

  - top_coins (string, optional): Market cap filter. Options: "300", "500", "1000", "all". Default: "1000".. Values: 300, 500, 1000, all.
